[SM-2722] Combustion leak (block) test. On 2010-2015 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself, and use fresh fluid for each test. A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.
[SEC 10.25] Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan. Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 3.4L V6 and 5.5L V8 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.
[B-22-172] Combustion leak (block) test. On 2016-2021 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself, and use fresh fluid for each test. Our family's 2018 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6 and the auto trans, just past 51k miles. The coolant level drops slowly between oil changes. I can't see any leak, there's no sweet smell inside, and it never runs hot. What's a sensible first test here?

With the 2018's V6 warmed up and idling, take off the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the blue test fluid, keeping the fluid out of the coolant itself [B-22-172]. If the fluid stays blue, there's no sign of combustion gases; a shift to yellow or green means they're getting into the cooling system.

After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. Charging and battery health both checked out on your 2016 sedan, so a circuit staying awake while it sits at the airport lot is what this measurement looks for.
